### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/README.md`, `packages/runtime/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/manifest.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/plugins/index.mdx`  _(via os plugin install (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/install.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via objectstack.plugin.json (literal, a string literal in COMPILED_PLUGIN_MANIFEST_FILE; a string literal in MANIFEST_FILE), os plugin build (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/build.ts), os plugin install (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/install.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via objectstack.plugin.json (literal, a string literal in COMPILED_PLUGIN_MANIFEST_FILE; a string literal in MANIFEST_FILE), os plugin build (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/build.ts))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via os plugin build (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/build.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/README.md`, `packages/runtime/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/manifest.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cb074ec3b35d69a1b98fe62ea23d77b8b6051f0c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e11734e0f17b7567db99f90301b26588e1118566` — the merge of head `f9521e4fc03120931867cd0361bff810a075d93a` into base `cb074ec3b35d69a1b98fe62ea23d77b8b6051f0c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e11734e0f17b7567db99f90301b26588e1118566 && git checkout e11734e0f17b7567db99f90301b26588e1118566
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cb074ec3b35d69a1b98fe62ea23d77b8b6051f0c f9521e4fc03120931867cd0361bff810a075d93a && git checkout -B drift-repro cb074ec3b35d69a1b98fe62ea23d77b8b6051f0c && git merge --no-ff f9521e4fc03120931867cd0361bff810a075d93a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cb074ec3b35d69a1b98fe62ea23d77b8b6051f0c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cb074ec3b35d69a1b98fe62ea23d77b8b6051f0c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a03c314054d907f9938deb310bb658166eb12fc6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/install.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/build.ts, packages/runtime/src/compiled-plugin-manifest.ts, packages/runtime/src/index.ts, packages/runtime/src/installed-plugin-loader.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/install.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.one-shot-family.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/test/json-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts, packages/cli/test/plugin-build-bundled-only.test.ts, packages/cli/test/serve-installed-plugins.integration.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/installed-plugin-loader.test.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest-packaging-retirement.test.ts + packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts (`ManifestSchema`, `PluginPackagingSchema`, `PACKAGING_RETIRED`, `PluginIntegritySchema`), packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key.ts (`enumWithRetiredValues`), packages/spec/src/shared/error-map.zod.ts (`formatZodIssue`), packages/core/src/security/plugin-artifact-integrity.ts (`verifyIntegrity`), packages/cli/src/utils/osplugin.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/plugin-install.ts (`materializePlugin`), packages/runtime/package.json (`exports`), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs (the `Clause-②` reader)

Face: narrowing — the PR body and the committed changeset both carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; no schema and no governed path in the file list. Read: card #27686 body and every comment (triage 6504372423, the seat's claim 6509288230 with its two surface amendments, the dev report 6511301044 as a claim to verify); PR #27791 body, 14-file list, net diff of `a03c3140` against its merge base `81d00a4e` on `main`, and its three comments; merged PR #27679 for how `ManifestSchema` carries the retirement. Check-runs on `a03c3140` at 2026-10-30T00:04Z: 48 runs, all completed, every one `success` or `skipped` (Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards and all eight Test Core shards among the successes; the skips are opt-in and matrix placeholders). Earlier readings during this review had Test Core 2/8 through 7/8 `in_progress`; the final reading is the one recorded. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was built, run or re-run here. The dev's ablation and gate counts are its claim, not evidence.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`os plugin install` refuses an invalid compiled manifest before anything is written — narrowing, real.** `install.ts` step 2 calls `readCompiledPluginManifest(files)` right after `archiveEntryProblems` and before `pluginInstallDir`, `verifyIntegrity` (step 3) and `materializePlugin`; `refuse()` only emits JSON or prints and exits, so on `manifest_invalid` no byte reaches the plugin home and no record is written (the install pin asserts the directory is absent). The hand-rolled `manifest_incomplete` (`id`/`version` by hand) and `integrity_malformed` (shape by hand) refusals are deleted: both facts are now `ManifestSchema` issues, so neither door keeps a second copy of a manifest rule. The read sits after signature verification over the raw bytes (step 1), which is the right order — untrusted bytes are not parsed before the key is checked. Accept-set change: a compiled manifest that is not a `ManifestSchema` manifest (retired `packaging` value, missing `name`/`type`, unknown key under `strictObject`, bad `id` pattern, non-SemVer `version`, non-record `integrity`) installed on `main` and is refused here. Declared as BREAKING on both carriers. Judged right.
2. **Boot loader, check 4: reported reason becomes the schema's message, still non-fatal.** `checkRecord` returns `refuse('manifest_invalid', ...)` through the same `Check` channel as every other refusal, before `dispatchPluginRuntime` and before any `import()`; `verifyInstalledPlugins` / `loadInstalledPlugins` keep going to the next record (the `com.acme.fine` pin and the real `os serve` boot pin, exit 0). `unreadable` keeps `artifact_unreadable`, so the only code that moves is a schema refusal, which on `main` surfaced later as `import_failed`. `manifest_invalid` is added to `InstalledPluginRefusalCode`; the one consumer outside the loader (`packages/cli/src/utils/installed-plugins-boot.ts`) prints `error` generically, no exhaustive map to update. Judged right, and it is what triage 6504372423 ordered.
3. **`packages/runtime/src/index.ts` widens `@objectstack/runtime`'s published surface — and the declaration does not say so.** `packages/runtime/package.json` has one `exports` entry, `.` → `dist/index.js`; the diff adds `export { readCompiledPluginManifest }` and `export type { CompiledPluginManifestRead }` to that entry (neither existed at the merge base; the helper file is new). The export is a design necessity — `packages/cli` can only reach a runtime helper through the package root, and the "one helper for both doors" ruling puts it in runtime — so the code is right and the **declaration is wrong**: the `Clause-②` value answers 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」, and a new named export on a published package's root entry enlarges the public surface, so the truthful value is `yes`. The fleet's one reader (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, "The four combinations") spells a diff that widens one surface and narrows another as **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`** — both facts read, the narrowing face and this tier unchanged, the level still at least `minor` (which the changeset already has). The PR body and the changeset both read `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. **Must-fix (②/declaration):** change the line on BOTH carriers to `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` and the levels stay. (The seat's own claim 6509288230 carried `no (narrowing)` before the dev placed the helper in runtime; the dev report names the export and still left the line.)
4. **`build.ts` native-addon refusal names the importer chain.** `packageImporters` lists files outside the package that import into it, and a breadth-first walk from the plugin's own inputs (those with no `node_modules` root) to the first file inside the package, collapsed to one step per package name; the line gains `, imported by …` and ` (reached through a → b → c)` only when there is something to say (a chain of two or more steps), so the direct-hit line is unchanged. The `.node`-module branch above it was already naming importers; this brings the package branch to parity. `metafile.inputs[i]!` is safe (`i` comes from `Object.keys(metafile.inputs)`); `imp.path in metafile.inputs` guards external imports. Pinned by the `ws-like → fake-native` case, which also asserts `ws-like` is never itself named native. Judged right; no accept-set change (what was refused is refused, with more words).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27686-plugin-install-parses-compiled-manifest.md`: `@objectstack/cli: minor`, `@objectstack/runtime: minor`. Packages the diff publishes: `packages/cli` and `packages/runtime` — matches (`packages/spec` and `packages/core` are only read; the spec edit is a test file, which publishes nothing). `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` → kind takes at least `minor` on both moved packages — consistent. `narrowed` is the right kind: a requirement on what an author's compiled `objectstack.plugin.json` must satisfy is tightened at two doors (nothing in `ManifestSchema` itself moves, as the changeset says).
- BREAKING banner present (`**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing …`), title `fix(cli)!`, FROM → TO remedy in the body (fix the source manifest as the refusal says, rebuild, sign, install). ADR-0087 disposition: exactly one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — honest here: no key is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped and `migrate meta` has nothing new to rewrite (PR #27679 already registered the D2 conversion for the value itself); `check:adr-0087-registration` ran green in the Lint gates.
- `Clause-②` / `Metadata-protocol` lines are present and byte-identical on the PR body and the changeset — consistent with each other, and **both wrong in the same way** (①.3): must read `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. The level is unaffected by the fix.
- Prose contradiction check: `packages/cli/README.md` install paragraph now names `manifest_invalid` with the schema's own message — agrees with the code; the PR body's `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` is superseded by comment 6510905884, which the seat's amended surface covers.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report `open_questions: []`; deviations: (a) PR opened without assignees — procedural, no bearing on the diff; (b) surface grown twice by seat amendment — both amendments are on the card (6509288230) before the commits that used them (75f26118 README, a03c3140 spec test). No stop-on-breach is owed.
- **Spec test edit (seat-approved, test-only):** three `EXCLUDED` entries in `manifest-packaging-retirement.test.ts`. Read each file: `install.integration.test.ts` authors `packaging: 'manifest-deps'` once, inside the pin asserting `manifest_invalid` and the prescription; `installed-plugin-loader.test.ts` twice, both inside refusal pins (table row and the "never imported, next plugin loads" case); `serve-installed-plugins.integration.test.ts` once, in `beforeAll` laying down a pre-retirement install whose only assertions are that boot refuses it as `manifest_invalid`, never `import_failed`, and never runs its `init`. Each reason holds. The walk's exclusion is file-level (same mechanism and granularity as the existing build-door pin entry); the anti-vacuity bounds (more than 1000 files visited, more than 3 authoring a packaging value) are untouched by three files, so the guard is not weakened otherwise.
- **`schema-migrate.one-shot-family.integration.test.ts` and `json-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts`:** each gains one fixture line, `name: …`. Both drive a real `os plugin install` on a hand-assembled artifact whose manifest lacked `name` — a required `ManifestSchema` key — so the narrowing itself turns them red; the fix makes the fixtures what `os plugin build` would have produced. They are tests of the install door and fall under the claim's "their tests"; naming them: a consequence of the narrowing, inside the surface, not a scope creep. (That two in-repo fixtures were never `ManifestSchema` manifests is itself evidence that the gap the card names was real.)
- **Stale evidence prose this PR leaves behind (should-fix, follow-up carrier):** `packages/spec/liveness/manifest.json:307` (the `integrity` row's evidence) and `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json:1802` both still name `integrity_malformed` as an `os plugin install` refusal; this PR deletes that code (it is a `manifest_invalid` schema issue now). `Spec property liveness` passed because it checks the `install.ts#PluginInstall` anchor, not the prose. The claim forbids `packages/spec` edits beyond the test file, so this is either a seat amendment or a follow-up card — not a landing blocker.
- **A third hand reader of the compiled manifest remains**, outside the ruling: `packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts` (step 2) and `readOspluginManifest` in `packages/cli/src/utils/osplugin.ts` still `JSON.parse` the compiled manifest and read `id`/`version`/`name` by hand. Triage named two doors (install, boot) and this PR delivers exactly those; the publish preflight is a candidate for the same helper. Noted for a follow-up card, not a fix here.

### ④ Design judgment

- **Against the published spec on `main`:** `ManifestSchema` (`packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts`, unchanged by this PR — verified by diff) is a `strictObject` whose `packaging` is `enumWithRetiredValues(['bundled'], PACKAGING_RETIRED)`; the retired member's prescription is the enum's own error message at path `packaging` (PR #27679 landed that; `formatZodIssue` renders it `✗ packaging: …`). This PR makes that refusal real at two doors that bypassed it; it takes no declared capability away at the consumer — nothing a valid manifest declares is refused that `main`'s `os plugin build` would accept.
- **One helper, no second copy:** `readCompiledPluginManifest` is the only `ManifestSchema.safeParse` of the compiled manifest; both doors map its three-way answer (`ok` / `unreadable` / `invalid`) onto their own channels and nothing else. The `manifest_mismatch` compare in the loader and `verifyIntegrity` in install consume the parsed value. Holds.
- **Break attempts, read:**
  - *A valid artifact built by current `os plugin build` must still install.* `build.ts` writes `{ ...parsed.data, main: 'dist/index.mjs', integrity }` — the schema's own OUTPUT plus two declared optional keys. `ManifestSchema` has no `.transform`/`.preprocess`/`.refine`; the only output-vs-input differences are defaults (`scope: 'project'`, `defaultDatasource: 'default'`), both of which re-parse; `main` is a plain optional string, `integrity` is `z.record(string, string)` and `computeIntegrity` yields exactly that. So the compiled manifest round-trips. Pinned live by the boot test's `os plugin build` artifact (`com.acme.built`) installing and loading.
  - *Build-only keys in a compiled manifest.* There are none: the compiled manifest is the parsed source manifest plus `main` and `integrity`, both declared on `ManifestSchema` for precisely this reason (the `main` docblock says so). A manifest carrying a key the schema does not declare was never a `ManifestSchema` manifest; refusing it is the declared narrowing.
  - *Refusal before any byte is written.* Confirmed in ①.1: the parse precedes `pluginInstallDir`, the integrity step, the lock and `materializePlugin`; `refuse()` touches no disk.
  - *Boot refusal of an already-installed stale plugin.* The realistic upgrade case — a record laid down by the old install for a `manifest-deps` artifact — is pinned by the real `os serve` boot test (`materializePlugin` + `recordPluginInstallation`), refused by name with the prescription, boot exit 0, next plugin loaded.
  - *Message rendering.* The helper strips `✗` and trims each `formatZodIssue` line, so nested union branches lose their indentation (flattened list). Cosmetic; the `path: message` form the pins assert survives. Not a fix.
- **Findings:** one must-fix (①.3, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on both carriers); one should-fix (③, stale `integrity_malformed` evidence prose in `packages/spec/liveness/manifest.json` and `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json`). The code holds; the declaration does not.

## Contract review

Head-sha: `f9521e4fc03120931867cd0361bff810a075d93a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/27686-plugin-install-parses-compiled-manifest.md, packages/spec/liveness/manifest.json, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json + scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs (`readClause2Line`, `readArmToken`), scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs (`reviewFace`), scripts/pm/check-owed-reviews.mjs (`owedFace`), scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs (`recordVerdict`), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (`declarationFromPullRequest`, `judgeLevel`), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/release-github-releases.mjs (`classifyReleaseBullet`), scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs and scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs (the `--body` / `issue_patch` route), packages/runtime/src/index.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/install.ts

Everything judged PASS-worthy in 6511494551 on the code (①.1, ①.2, ①.4, ④) is unchanged by this delta and is adopted, not re-argued. Check-runs on `f9521e4f` at 2026-10-30T00:22Z: 48 runs; 24 `success`, 10 `skipped`, 14 still `in_progress` (Build & E2E UI, Build Core, Live E2E UI, Test Core (1/8), Test Core (2/8), Test Core (3/8), Test Core (4/8), Test Core (5/8), Test Core (6/8), Test Core (7/8), Test Core (8/8), Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace); no run has failed. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts; a run still in progress is recorded as such. Nothing was built, run or re-run here; the dev's "all exit 0" list in 6511632334 is its claim, not evidence.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The must-fix (①.3 of 6511494551) is answered on the committed carrier.** The changeset now reads `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` / `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, and its "Now." bullet names the widening by its two members: `readCompiledPluginManifest` and `CompiledPluginManifestRead`, new named exports of `@objectstack/runtime`'s root entry (the only `exports` entry of that package) — exactly the widening the record found, no more and no less (`packages/runtime/src/index.ts` is untouched by the delta and still adds those two names only).
